instruction: Delete the last slide from this presentation. The presentation currently has 28 slides.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to change all text fonts to Liberation Sans Narrow via master slide editing. Spent 50 turns editing individual template elements in master slide view and tried Find & Replace, but failed to change fonts across all text boxes.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Impress UI, enter master slide view, select text, change font properties in Character panel, use keyboard shortcuts like Ctrl+H
metadata.failure_analysis: Model edited master slide template elements one-by-one instead of using a bulk method. Got confused between font variants. Find & Replace cannot change fonts. Task limit reached at 50 turns.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a basic slide management task (deleting a slide). Model demonstrated it can see and interact with the slide panel. Right-clicking a slide thumbnail and selecting Delete is a simple operation.
metadata.explanation: Task requires deleting the last slide (slide 28) from the presentation. Evaluator counts slides in the saved pptx and checks if count equals 27.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly downloads the pptx file from the VM and counts slides using python-pptx library
Metric correctly accesses expected.get('expected_count') — proper handling for type='rule' where expected IS the rules dict
Expected value of 27 is correct (28 slides minus 1 deleted = 27)
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state

Minor limitation: evaluator only verifies slide count equals 27, not that the specifically deleted slide was the last one (slide 28). Deleting any single slide would also pass. However, this is a reasonable approximation for this simple task.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: To fully verify 'last slide deleted', could additionally check that the content of slides 1-27 matches the original slides 1-27 (confirming the last slide was removed, not an arbitrary one). However, this level of verification may be overkill for an easy task.
